report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **supported by robust clinical evidence**. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses confirm that anti-cytokine drugs significantly reduce depressive symptoms in people with chronic inflammatory conditions.

### Supporting Evidence
* **Effectiveness in Chronic Illness:** Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating anti-cytokine biologics (such as anti-TNF and anti-IL-6 agents) in autoimmune diseases—including psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease—demonstrate small-to-moderate reductions in depressive symptoms [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/], [https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/anti-inflammatory-drugs-could-treat-symptoms-of-depression].
* **Independent Antidepressant Effects:** Statistical mediation analyses show that mood improvements are not solely due to relief from pain or physical disability; anti-cytokine drugs exert direct antidepressant effects by targeting immune-to-brain inflammatory pathways [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/].

### Counter-Evidence and Limitations
* **Inflammation Dependency:** Clinical trials in general major depressive disorder show that anti-cytokine agents fail to improve mood in depressed individuals lacking systemic inflammation. Therapeutic benefits are restricted specifically to patients with elevated baseline inflammatory biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein [https://www.healio.com/news/psychiatry/20181026/immunebrain-interaction-may-shed-light-on-major-depression].
* **Safety and Feasibility:** Risks of immunosuppression, serious infections, high cost, and route of administration prevent anti-cytokine drugs from being used as standard first-line antidepressants for psychiatric populations overall [https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/anti-inflammatory-drugs-could-treat-symptoms-of-depression].

### Sources
1. PMC Meta-Analysis on Anti-Cytokines: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/
2. Pharmaceutical Journal Overview: https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/anti-inflammatory-drugs-could-treat-symptoms-of-depression
3. Healio Psychiatry Report on Immune-Brain Interactions: https://www.healio.com/news/psychiatry/20181026/immunebrain-interaction-may-shed-light-on-major-depression
